meta.move: Written by the lead after attempt 1 (not blind): owns the zero, shows each piece by saying so, answers each defence in a sentence, offers 4.4, sets a date
meta.expect: She reaches the deal after Hale offers 4.4; she never proposes the rewrite herself

turns.text: Hello, thanks for coming in. I'm Owen's English teacher.
Why am I here, Hale? A zero went into the gradebook before anyone called me.
Thanks for coming in. Before anything else: I entered the zero on November 3 without calling you first. That was wrong, and Owen shouldn't have found out on his phone.
Okay. Go on.

I've turned my laptop to you. This is the document's version history: created Wednesday, October 28, at 11:31 PM with a title only. At 11:52 PM, 612 words appear in one edit. At 11:58 PM, another 794 words in one edit. No earlier drafts.
I'm writing those times down. People draft elsewhere and paste it in, so what does 4.3 say about that?
If he drafted it somewhere else, he can bring that draft with its date and I'll look at it. Until then, this record is what we have.
He told me he wrote it over the weekend. Fine, he can be asked for a draft. Is anything on his record right now?
Here's the essay, page two, and here's the play open to Act 3, Scene 2. The essay quotes 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile.' Search the scene yourself; it isn't there.
Students misquote plays all the time. Is a wrong line what the zero was entered for?
A misquote from memory is usually close to a real line. This one isn't close to anything in the play.
Fine. It isn't in the play. What else is there, and what are you proposing for his record?
Here's his October 15 outline beside the essay. The outline argues Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay argues epistemological paralysis and never mentions cowardice.
An outline is a starting point, and students change their argument as they write. Isn't that what revising is?

Here's what I can offer under procedure 4.4: a private supervised rewrite, after school, not in front of his class, before December 1. The new mark replaces the zero, and nothing goes on his record. I'll put that in writing tonight.
Okay. Private, nothing on his record, in writing tonight. I'm agreeing to put this behind him, not because he did anything.
Thursday the twelfth after school works for me. Does that work for Owen?
I'll confirm with him tonight. Put the date and the time in the email.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

You agreed to a private supervised rewrite after school on Thursday the twelfth, its mark replacing the zero, with nothing placed on Owen's record. I still want the date and time of the rewrite and the promise about his record in that email, in writing. I expect it tonight.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: Last position: she accepted a private supervised rewrite on Thursday the twelfth that replaces the zero with nothing on his record, and she still wants the written confirmation tonight with the date and time; that is the fair outcome under procedure 4.4, and her time did not run out first.
What moved her: You offered the rewrite with every condition she cared about, private, replacing the zero and nothing on file, after she had seen your documents, so it answered her biggest fear directly.
What cost ground: Nothing.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your version history with its late-night times on the night before the essay was due came closest to that night, though it proves nothing about the essay, and it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When she said students change their argument as they write, you moved straight to the rewrite, so answer that point first, for example by asking what in the essay still reflects the outline.
